previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for two weeks of diffuse abdominal pain and bilious vomiting, initially attributed to constipation. Imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology, and symptoms improved with bowel regimen and enemas, supporting opioid-induced constipation as the cause. A urine culture grew E. coli, leading to a three-day course of Bactrim for a mild UTI. Her INR was monitored due to Coumadin interaction. Chronic conditions including HIV, hepatitis B/C, diastolic heart failure, and a healing left tibial fracture were stable. Orthopedics cleared her for 50% weight-bearing. She was discharged home with services, instructed to complete antibiotics, monitor INR, follow up with orthopedics, and maintain bowel regimen.

___ with HIV, hx of migraines here with severe headache likely 
due to migraine along with leukocytosis and fever possibly due

ACTIVE ISSUES
# Headache: Patient presented with severe frontal headache 
accompanied by photophobia and nausea consistent with prior 
migraines. Patient had run out of her migraine medicine at home. 
However, in the setting of fevers and leukocytosis there was 
some concern for meningitis. Patient adamantly refused lumbar 
puncture despite being notified of the risks/benefits of the 
procedure, so she was started presumptively on ceftriaxone, 
moxifloxacin, ampicillin, and acyclovir. After receiving a dose 
of imitrex, patient's headache improved substantially. As there 
were felt to be other sources of her fever/leukocytosis (see 
below), meningitis therapy was discontinued by HD#2 after 
consulting with ID.
.
# Cellulitis: Left lower leg with erythema, swelling, tenderness 
and scab serving as likely portal of entry consistent with 
cellulitis. This was thought to be the most likely source of her 
fevers and white count. Discharged on bactrim and cepalexin for 
a seven day course. Blood cultures were pending at the time of 
discharge. 
.
# UTI: Initially, patient endorse dysuria and suprapubic 
tenderness but was inconsistent in her reporting. Urine culture 
grew E.coli sensitive to Bactrim so patient was discharged on 
seven day course of this antibiotic, as above.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ with cough, fever, dysuria, and abdominal pain,
assess for pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

AP AND LATERAL RADIOGRAPHS OF THE CHEST:  No focal consolidation is seen in
the lungs, with likely bibasilar scarring and linear mid lung atelectasis. 
The lateral view is suboptimal, but does not reveal evidence of a pleural
effusion.  No pneumothorax is seen.  The heart is likely normal in size with
tortuous thoracic aorta.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study without evidence of acute process.

INDICATION:  ___ with HIV and obesity with headache, assess for acute
process.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect or
major vascular territorial infarction.  There is no shift of normally midline
structures.  Ventricles and sulci are prominent, compatible with age-related
involutional changes.  Gray-white matter differentiation is preserved with
focal hypodensities in the right basal ganglia, likely reflecting a prominent
VR space and unchanged from previous study.  Mucosal thickening is seen in the
right nasal cavity and ethmoid air cells.  Otherwise, paranasal sinuses and
mastoid air cells are well aerated.  No fracture is seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

microbiology.comments: HIV-1 RNA is not detected.  Performed using the ___ HIV-1 Test v2.0.  Detection Range: 20-10,000,000 copies/mL.  This test is approved for monitoring HIV-1 viral load in known HIV-positive patients. It is not approved for diagnosis of acute HIV infection.  In symptomatic acute HIV infection (acute retroviral syndrome), the viral load is usually very high (>>1000 copies/mL). If acute HIV infection is clinically suspected and there is a detectable but low viral load, please contact the laboratory for interpretation.  It is recommended that any NEW positive HIV-1 viral load result, in the absence of positive serology, be confirmed by submitting a new sample FOR HIV-1 PCR, in addition to serological testing.
